advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make §2c distinguish a failed `du` measurement from a genuine small size (check du's exit status / non-empty capture) instead of defaulting an unmeasured entry to 0 bytes.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:192: `debris_names="${debris_names} ${name}"` — the entry is named regardless of whether its bytes were measured

ABSENCE: du's exit status is never inspected; there is no world-distinguishing signal between 'du measured 0/small' and 'du errored and defaulted to 0', so the debris total can silently under-report and keep the alarm below threshold
advisory.finding: The per-entry `du` measurement in §2c fails open: `du -sk` failures (permission denied on a subtree, transient error, empty output) are swallowed by `2>/dev/null` and the pipe, then `entry_kb=${entry_kb:-0}` substitutes 0. A debris entry that du cannot successfully measure is still NAMED in journald but contributes 0 bytes to `debris_bytes`, so the census cannot distinguish 'entry is genuinely small' from 'measurement failed' — and the 1 GiB `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-debris` alarm may never fire for real debris the probe could not size.
scenarios: A debris directory contains a subtree the probe's uid cannot stat; du prints a partial size or nothing, and the missing bytes are dropped from the alarm-relevant total
du transiently errors during a 5-minute tick, publishing a debris_bytes reading far below the true footprint

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the §2c glob (or use a `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` enumeration) so debris names beginning with two dots are not silently skipped.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_observability_data_disk_debris.py:170 comment: `A dotted directory is still debris; a glob that skipped it would be a silent hole.` — the test only covers single-dot names (`.epoch-probe-scratch`)
ABSENCE: no glob term matches names like `..foo`; `.[!.]*` requires the char after the first dot to be a non-dot
advisory.finding: The hidden-entry glob `"$DATA_MOUNT"/.[!.]*` matches names beginning with a single dot but NOT names beginning with two dots (e.g. `..evidence`); such an entry is matched by neither the `*` nor the `.[!.]*` glob and is silently skipped, contradicting the 'hidden entries are not missed' guarantee the test asserts.
scenarios: A shell writes debris to `/var/gerrit/..evidence` (a legal filename); the census never sees it and publishes a clean-looking reading

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make §2c distinguish a du failure from a genuinely-empty entry so unreadable debris does not silently count as 0 bytes (e.g. detect non-zero du exit and publish nothing / a sentinel rather than fold to 0).
evidence: The named-but-unmeasured path: line 192 appends `${name}` to debris_names regardless of du success, so an entry can appear in journald with the volume's debris_bytes not reflecting it.

Block comment intent (line 158-160): 'the guard is that such a write becomes VISIBLE within one probe interval instead of accumulating silently' — a du-failure-to-0 defeats this for unreadable debris.
advisory.finding: The §2c census silently undercounts debris when `du` fails on an entry: `entry_kb=$(du -sk "$entry" 2>/dev/null ...)` followed by `entry_kb=${entry_kb:-0}` treats any du failure (permission-denied, transient I/O error) as 0 bytes, so a real debris directory the probe cannot fully read contributes 0 to `debris_bytes` while still being named — the volume can hold >1 GiB of debris yet stay below the alarm threshold, reintroducing the silent-accumulation failure this guard exists to close.
scenarios: An evidence dump written by another uid/agent that the probe's user cannot fully stat; du emits a partial size or errors, undercounting
A transient I/O error on a large debris tree mid-census keeps debris_bytes under 1 GiB

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that overrides `DATA_DEBRIS_ALLOW` (e.g. include an extra keep name) and asserts the newly-allowed top-level entry is excluded from `data_disk_debris_bytes`, or correct the source comment's 'seam the tests drive' claim.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:168: `# DATA_DEBRIS_ALLOW is the seam the tests drive; it is not a production tuning knob.`

search_files for DATA_DEBRIS_ALLOW returns only the three occurrences inside observability.sh (lines 168, 175, 183); no occurrence in tests/scripts/test_observability_data_disk_debris.py or elsewhere in tests/
The `_environment` helper (lines 54-106) sets DATA_MOUNT and offset vars but never DATA_DEBRIS_ALLOW, so every test runs the default allow-list.
advisory.finding: The `DATA_DEBRIS_ALLOW` override is documented as 'the seam the tests drive' but no test in the suite sets it; the allow-list matching loop is only ever exercised with the default `site lost+found`, so a regression in custom-allow-list word-splitting or multi-entry matching would go undetected and the comment's claim is untrue.
scenarios: A future edit adds a top-level consumer to DATA_DEBRIS_ALLOW and mis-splits the value (e.g. quoting), silently allow-listing everything; no test would catch it.
The comment claiming tests drive the seam misleads a maintainer into assuming override coverage exists.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that sets `env['DATA_DEBRIS_ALLOW'] = 'site lost+found scratch'`, plants `scratch/` plus a debris dir, and asserts only the debris dir is counted and named — exercising the allow-list word-split with a non-default value.
